basis.governing_question: Should Quinta Azul enter the Spanish retail market and, if so, how?

sub_questions.question: How large and attractive is the Spanish retail market for olive oil?
Who competes in Spanish retail, and what do its buyers and shoppers need from an olive-oil supplier?
Does Quinta Azul have the assets and capabilities to win in Spanish retail?
Which ways of entering Spanish retail are open to Quinta Azul, and how do they compare?
On the evidence and the business case, should Quinta Azul go or not go into Spain?
If go, what entry plan sequences the steps from first contact with buyers to the first listing?

work.unit: Market assessed in full (demand, channels, competitors, regulation, buyer interviews)

phase_work.why: Spain is the only market named, so it is assessed in full with no desk screen; capability gap work runs alongside.

work.unit: Entry option and business case for one market
Entry sequence and roadmap across markets

phase_work.why: Business case for the one market first, then the roadmap that carries the entry plan; both fit the typical 3 to 6 weeks.

sizing.levers: Narrowing buyer interviews in Research to a few Spanish chains, and keeping the entry roadmap to an outline, would shorten the engagement most.

phases.name: Research
phases.objective_one_line: Assess the Spanish retail market, its competitors and buyers, and Quinta Azul's capability to win there.

gate.label: Go/no-go on design
gate.decision: Go or no-go on designing an entry plan for the Spanish retail market?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Compare entry options, test the business case, and set out an entry plan if the answer is go.

gate.label: Final decision
gate.decision: Approve the go or no-go call on Spain and, if go, the entry plan?

architect_notes: No engagement length was given; the 7 to 10 weeks is an estimate from the sizing, to be confirmed before quoting.
Design runs only on a go at the Research gate, so a no-go there ends the engagement after 4 to 5 weeks.
